review_notes: I read the whole of BaseChange.lean. I also read the other `toFDRepIso` and `isoToEquiv` sites and the group-algebra call site, but only through grep context windows. I did not open the other files in full. I found no repeated block in this file that is nontrivial enough to justify a shared lemma. `baseChangeK0_id` and `baseChangeK0_comp` both finish with "rewrite `FDRep.of_ρ'`, rewrite `baseChange_apply`, then induct on tensors". Their simp closers differ, though, and `comp` needs a nested induction. They also share the pattern with `baseChangeFDRepUnitIso` and `baseChangeFDRepTensorIso` in the other file. Each instance is a short, case-specific calculation, so I did not propose a missed finding.

claims.reason: The repeated material is about two lines of routine unfolding: `rw [FDRep.of_ρ', FDRep.of_ρ']` followed by `exact IntertwiningMap.isIntertwining _ _ e.toIntertwiningMap g x`. It is not nontrivial mathematical reasoning. The proposed `Representation.Equiv.toFDRepIso` would be a thin wrapper around the existing `LinearEquiv.toFDRepIso` plus `IntertwiningMap.isIntertwining`. The rubric says thin wrappers and routine unfolding are insufficient. The two call sites are also not identical. The group-algebra one uses `simpa only [FDRep.of_ρ', Equiv.toLinearEquiv_apply]` with a `let e` whose carriers are built from `indFDRepForgetEquiv`. Here the target is `rw [FDRep.of_ρ', FDRep.of_ρ']` on an `FDRep.of` object. With only two uses, the helper would save a couple of lines per site, which is a convenience API addition and not the removal of duplicated proof machinery. The group-algebra file is also outside the reviewed file, and I did not check that a shared helper there would be free of import or dependency problems.
